title: And / but / because
note: Basic linkers. Gap on and / but / because only. and=add · but=opposite · because=why. Soft accepts where natural (stay home / stay at home). · 2026-08-29 smoke: Remember + Examples recap cut (C17); C13 bold the linker on every card; C14 title_cz without 'linkers'; C19 Job column English only; authored chips and/but/because (C11 no so/or); F3 Homare/Tomas/writes/strong/sunny/sits relexified onto Martina/Anna + taught vocab; A8 contractions; D1 item-shaped explanations. · folded in from retired core_frames vocab trunk 2026-08-31 (or · so)

items.en: Klara likes English and Czech.
items.cz: Klára má ráda angličtinu a češtinu.
accepts: Klara likes English and Czech.
items.explanation: **and** adds Czech next to English.
items.explanation_cz: **and** přidává češtinu k angličtině.

items.en: We work and study.
accepts: We work and study.
items.explanation: **and** adds a second action: work **and** study.
items.explanation_cz: **and** přidává druhou činnost: work **and** study.

items.en: Tereza likes tea and coffee.
items.cz: Tereza má ráda čaj a kávu.
accepts: Tereza likes tea and coffee.
items.explanation: **and** adds coffee next to tea.
items.explanation_cz: **and** přidává kávu k čaji.

items.en: They eat bread and cheese.
accepts: They eat bread and cheese.
items.explanation: **and** adds cheese next to bread.
items.explanation_cz: **and** přidává sýr k chlebu.

items.en: She has a bag and a book.
items.gap: She has a bag ____ a book.
accepts: She has a bag and a book.
items.explanation: **and** adds a book next to a bag.
items.explanation_cz: **and** přidává knihu k tašce.

items.en: He reads and works.
accepts: He reads and works.
items.explanation: **and** adds a second action: reads **and** works.
items.explanation_cz: **and** přidává druhou činnost: reads **and** works.

items.en: I want milk and water.
accepts: I want milk and water.
items.explanation: **and** adds water next to milk.
items.explanation_cz: **and** přidává vodu k mléku.

items.en: They play football and tennis.
accepts: They play football and tennis.
They play soccer and tennis.
items.explanation: **and** adds tennis next to football.
items.explanation_cz: **and** přidává tenis k fotbalu.

items.en: She is tired but happy.
accepts: She is tired but happy.
She's tired but happy.
items.explanation: **but** shows the opposite feeling: tired **but** happy.
items.explanation_cz: **but** ukazuje opak: tired **but** happy.

items.en: He is hungry but he can help.
items.cz: On má hlad, ale může pomoct.
items.gap: He is hungry ____ he can help.
accepts: He is hungry but he can help.
He's hungry but he can help.
items.explanation: **but** is the surprise: hungry **but** he can help.
items.explanation_cz: **but** je to překvapení: hungry **but** he can help.

items.en: I want coffee but I have tea.
items.gap: I want coffee ____ I have tea.
accepts: I want coffee but I have tea.
items.explanation: **but** shows the opposite: I want coffee **but** I have tea.
items.explanation_cz: **but** ukazuje opak: I want coffee **but** I have tea.

items.en: It rains but we play football.
accepts: It rains but we play football.
It rains but we play soccer.
It is raining but we play football.
It's raining but we play football.
It is raining but we play soccer.
It's raining but we play soccer.
items.explanation: **but** is the surprise: it rains **but** we play.
items.explanation_cz: **but** je to překvapení: it rains **but** we play.

items.en: She is busy but she can help.
items.cz: Ona má hodně práce, ale může pomoct.
items.gap: She is busy ____ she can help.
accepts: She is busy but she can help.
She's busy but she can help.
She has a lot of work but she can help.
items.explanation: **but** is the surprise: busy **but** she can help.
items.explanation_cz: **but** je to překvapení: busy **but** she can help.

items.en: I like dogs but I don't like cats.
items.cz: Mám rád psy, ale nemám rád kočky.
items.gap: I like dogs ____ I don't like cats.
accepts: I like dogs but I don't like cats.
I like dogs but I do not like cats.
items.explanation: **but** shows the opposite: dogs **but** not cats.
items.explanation_cz: **but** ukazuje opak: dogs **but** not cats.

items.en: Lenka is tired but she works.
accepts: Lenka is tired but she works.
items.explanation: **but** is the surprise: tired **but** she works.
items.explanation_cz: **but** je to překvapení: tired **but** she works.

items.en: They are busy but happy.
items.cz: Oni mají hodně práce, ale jsou šťastní.
accepts: They are busy but happy.
They're busy but happy.
They are busy but they are happy.
They're busy but they're happy.
items.explanation: **but** shows the opposite: busy **but** happy.
items.explanation_cz: **but** ukazuje opak: busy **but** happy.

items.en: I stay home because I am tired.
items.gap: I stay home ____ I am tired.
accepts: I stay home because I am tired.
I stay at home because I am tired.
I stay home because I'm tired.
I stay at home because I'm tired.
items.explanation: **because** says why I stay home: I am tired.
items.explanation_cz: **because** říká proč zůstávám doma: I am tired.

items.en: I drink water because I am thirsty.
items.gap: I drink water ____ I am thirsty.
accepts: I drink water because I am thirsty.
I drink water because I'm thirsty.
items.explanation: **because** says why I drink water: I am thirsty.
items.explanation_cz: **because** říká proč piju vodu: I am thirsty.

items.en: She is at home because it is late.
items.cz: Ona je doma, protože je pozdě.
items.gap: She is at home ____ it is late.
accepts: She is at home because it is late.
She is at home because it's late.
She's at home because it is late.
She's at home because it's late.
She is home because it is late.
She is home because it's late.
She's home because it is late.
She's home because it's late.
items.explanation: **because** says why she is at home: it is late.
items.explanation_cz: **because** říká proč je doma: it is late.

items.en: I sit down because I am tired.
items.gap: I sit down ____ I am tired.
accepts: I sit down because I am tired.
I sit down because I'm tired.
items.explanation: **because** says why I sit down: I am tired.
items.explanation_cz: **because** říká proč si sedám: I am tired.

items.en: We go home because it is cold.
items.gap: We go home ____ it is cold.
accepts: We go home because it is cold.
We go home because it's cold.
items.explanation: **because** says why we go home: it is cold.
items.explanation_cz: **because** říká proč jdeme domů: it is cold.

items.en: I eat because I am hungry.
accepts: I eat because I am hungry.
I eat because I'm hungry.
items.explanation: **because** says why I eat: I am hungry.
items.explanation_cz: **because** říká proč jím: I am hungry.

items.en: She opens the window because it is hot.
items.cz: Ona otevírá okno, protože je horko.
items.gap: She opens the window ____ it is hot.
accepts: She opens the window because it is hot.
She opens the window because it's hot.
She opens a window because it is hot.
She opens a window because it's hot.
items.explanation: **because** says why she opens the window: it is hot.
items.explanation_cz: **because** říká proč otevírá okno: it is hot.

items.en: They stay home because it rains.
accepts: They stay home because it rains.
They stay at home because it rains.
They stay home because it is raining.
They stay at home because it is raining.
They stay home because it's raining.
They stay at home because it's raining.
items.explanation: **because** says why they stay home: it rains.
items.explanation_cz: **because** říká proč zůstávají doma: it rains.

items.en: Do you want tea or coffee?
accepts: Do you want tea or coffee
Do you want tea or coffee?
items.explanation: **or** = a choice between two.
items.explanation_cz: **or** = nebo (volba ze dvou).

items.en: I am tired so I go to bed.
items.gap: I am tired ____ I go to bed.
accepts: I am tired so I go to bed
I'm tired so I go to bed.
items.explanation: **so** = the result. *because* gives the reason, **so** gives what follows.
items.explanation_cz: **so** = tak, proto (výsledek). *because* = důvod.

cards.title: And / but / because
points: These three words join two ideas.

examples.en: I stay home **because** I am tired.
I want coffee **but** I have tea.
I stay home **because** I am tired.
I drink water **because** I am thirsty.

cards.title: Which word?
points: Look at the job of the second part.
